title.narrative: Scaling the delivery of the luminos program within government school systems in Liberia and the Gambia

description.narrative: Pandemic-related school closures impacted 250 million students in sub-Saharan Africa, adding to the 100 million children consistently out of school prior to 2020. Hundreds of millions lost not only the opportunity to learn, but the future opportunity to earn, and millions may not set foot back in a classroom. To help get more children back into classrooms, the Luminos Fund developed a program that helps children catch up to grade level and return to school. Through its original model, Luminos trains community-based organizations to identify and recruit out-of-school children and engage them in a ten-month, activity-based curriculum. Luminos then helps children reintegrate into public school systems at age-appropriate grade levels. A 2018 longitudinal study found that around 90 percent of Luminos students transitioned to formal schools at the end of the program and 74 percent were still attending a year later. On average, Luminos students outperformed their peers in literacy and numeracy by ten percentage points. In the 2022-23 school year, with multi-donor funding, Luminos selected IDInsight to conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to rigorously evaluate the programs effectiveness. Support from Development Innovation Ventures will strengthen the ongoing RCT by enabling Luminos to track student enrollment, retention, and learning outcomes for a year beyond the end of the program. DIV will also support Luminos to provide technical assistance to the governments of Liberia and The Gambia to determine how public schools can directly implement the Luminos program. Luminos aims to reach 137,040 children and 2,302 teachers during the award period, and has the potential to reach millions of out-of-school children through government partnerships.

title.narrative: Using Machine Learning to Reduce HIV Treatment Interruptions

description.narrative: Approximately 39 million people were living with HIV/AIDS worldwide at the end of 2022. While great strides have been made in increasing access to treatment, interruption in treatment remains a persistent problem that can result in viral rebound, disease advancement, and premature mortality. A study in Akwa Ibom, Nigeria found the treatment retention rate for people living with HIV/AIDS to be just 68 percent after one year, significantly lower than the benchmark of 98 percent set by the Presidents Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) in Nigeria. To increase the treatment retention rate, FHI 360 developed and piloted a machine learning algorithm to identify people likely to interrupt treatment using patient data available through HIV/AIDS programs. Once the algorithm identifies people likely to interrupt treatment, providers can offer tailored care to address barriers that may prevent them from adhering to treatment. With support from Development Innovation Ventures and PEPFAR, FHI 360 will scale its program to 16,000 people across two Nigerian states and will conduct a randomized controlled trial to rigorously evaluate the effect of the program on measures of treatment interruption (e.g. missed appointments), patient viral loads, and patient satisfaction. This study will inform whether this machine learning approach can improve resource allocation and health outcomes and should ultimately be integrated into broader HIV/AIDS programming.

title.narrative: Evaluating and Optimizing the Impact of Pulas Insurance Products and Services

description.narrative: As climate change makes weather patterns more unpredictable, millions of smallholder farmers are increasingly vulnerable to droughts and other severe weather. However, basic agricultural insurance that could protect livelihoods against the effects of climate change is generally too expensive for farmers working less than two hectares (five acres) of land and living on less than $2 per day. To make insurance more accessible to smallholders, Pula Advisors sells insurance policies to governments and large farmer support programssuch as the Zambian Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP) or the World Food Programwhich, in turn, provide them to farmers as part of a social safety net bundle that may also include access to farming loans and inputs, such as high-quality seeds or fertilizer. Although the potential value of agricultural insurance products is significant, the effects of an affordable and commercially viable insurance product like Pulas have not yet been rigorously tested. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), Pula will conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate whether access to commercial insurance encourages farmers to invest in higher-quality inputs or equipment. DIV funding will also enable Pula to use satellite data to automate its risk models and improve the quality and accuracy of its data collected from farm visits, which is costly to gather and can be error-prone. The results of this award will inform public policy on the possible benefits of providing commercial-scale insurance as part of social support programs.

title.narrative: Testing the Soil Method to Sustainably Manage Fall Armyworm

description.narrative: Known for its ability to damage and destroy a wide variety of crops, the invasive fall armyworm pest is very difficult to manage. Smallholder farmers in Kenya have lost as much as 47 percent of their maize crops to fall armyworm infestations in a single season, putting their food security and income at serious risk. Despite the scale and impact of fall armyworm on staple crops, typical mitigation strategiessuch as pesticidesare unproven or difficult for smallholder farmers to adopt due to cost and lack of skills. To make effective fall armyworm control accessible, the implementing partner, a Kenyan social enterprise, is rigorously testing a low-cost preventative measure known as the soil method. Based on traditional farmer knowledge, the soil method is a simple agroecological intervention that requires farmers to place soil onto the whorl (new leaf growth) of a maize plant when the plant is vulnerable to fall armyworm infestation. This method has been used in different parts of the world, but it has not been validated through rigorous studies. The implementing partner will conduct trials in both greenhouse and field settings to determine whether the soil method reduces fall armyworm damage to maize crops and to assess Kenyan farmers perceptions of the approach. If found effective, results from the two studies will inform future research on how best to promote wide-scale adoption.

title.narrative: Piloting an Insect Approach to Address Malnutrition and Food Insecurity
Productivité du secteur privé

description.narrative: Food insecurity is a significant global challenge, particularly in Madagascar, which ranks 119 out of 121 countries on the Global Hunger Index. Across the island, eight million people are undernourished, leading to early deaths, preterm deliveries, low birth weights, and irreversible cognitive and developmental delays for babies and children. To help alleviate this hunger crisis, the implementing partner has created a high-protein, insect-based instant porridge formulation for distribution by emergency and development food assistance programs. The porridge, which contains dried cricket powder as a key ingredient, may provide more protein and iron per serving than other commonly used nutritional supplements and can be baked into a cracker, among other preparations. Dried cricket powder is entirely local, inexpensive to produce, and aligns with Madagascan dietary preferences, which traditionally include edible insects. The implementing partner will scientifically test and fine-tune its instant porridge recipe to verify that it contains the ideal ratio and combination of ingredients and meets international nutritional and safety guidelines to qualify for formal accreditation as a nutritional supplement. As part of this award, the team will finalize a scale-ready version of its porridge and develop a commercial strategy to bring the final product to a national market. Once the dried cricket instant porridge formulation is accredited, global humanitarian organizations will be able to purchase, use, and distribute it to millions of people in need of nutritional supplementation.

title.narrative: Introducing Improved Climate Insurance Products to Smallholder Coffee Farmers

description.narrative: The effects of climate change expose hundreds of millions of smallholder farmers to droughts and other severe weather that puts their livelihoods at risk. Insurance can help protect farmers against losses but is usually unavailable or too expensive for smallholders to purchase. With access to insurance, farmers are expected to have higher risk tolerance and be more likely to invest in farm inputs that can increase their productivity. The implementing partner offers seasonal climate insurance to protect smallholder farmers. To make insurance more affordable while still commercially viable, the implementing partner bases insurance payouts on predetermined, explicit conditions, called index insurance. Index insurance lowers claim processing costs and increases trust with smallholder farmers. The implementing partner also provides weather-prompted information and advice to farmers via mobile phones, such as guidance for dealing with unexpected weather patterns, to enable farmers to manage more climate risks independently. Satellite data and other digital tools help keep risk profile assessments and claim processing costs low as well. The implementing partner will introduce its suite of digital products through its Climate Smart CoffeeTM program, pilot them with 1,000 coffee farmers in Kenya, and conduct an impact study to understand whether coffee farmers incomes or investments have increased after obtaining this insurance. The implementing partner aims to reduce climate protection costs and increase on-farm investment, enabling smallholder farmers to improve their climate resilience and incomes.

title.narrative: Evaluating the Impact of a Comprehensive School Health Program

description.narrative: While many health programs focus on early childhood, the health needs of older children often go overlooked. Schoolchildren have the fewest touch points with the healthcare system of any age group, yet face serious health challenges; for example, children aged five to 17 experience the highest prevalence of malaria. To help bridge the gap between schooling and health, Zambian nonprofit Healthy Learners works with the Ministries of Health and Education to train teachers as school health workers (SHWs) and connect children to care. SHWs deliver health education in classrooms, use the ThinkMD clinical decision support system to assess students and make preliminary diagnoses, provide preventative care (such as deworming medication and vitamin supplementation) and care for mild conditions in Healthy Learners specially-constructed school health rooms, and make fast-track referrals to local clinics where students receive priority care. With support from Development Innovation Ventures and the London School of Economics, Healthy Learners will conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial to evaluate the programs impact on health and education outcomes compared to a simple deworming program and no intervention. The trial results will inform the continued scaling of the program, potential long-term Government of Zambia funding, and expansion to other countries.

title.narrative: Testing and Scaling an Artificial Intelligence-Based Functional Literacy Program
Produtividade do Setor Privado

description.narrative: Many of Brazils 28 million public school studentsespecially those from economically disadvantaged familiesare unprepared to attend university and enter the workforce. Nearly one-third of 15-to-64-year-old Brazilians are functionally illiterate, meaning they lack the reading, writing, and math skills required for everyday life. To help solve this literacy gap at scale, the implementing partner developed an artificial intelligence (AI)powered educational program that engages students in the classroom and supports teachers by providing specific, prompt feedback on writing submissions. The system goes beyond spelling and basic grammar to support students skills in diction, organization and flow, reading comprehension, and other aspects to promote functional literacy. A smaller-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) found that using the system in the final year of high school improved students essay scores on Brazils college entrance exam by 0.1 standard deviations (or 17 points out of a possible 1,000), compared with the control group, results that may reduce inequalities between public and private schools. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, the implementing partner will conduct a second RCT with 200,000 students to generate evidence on the programs longer-term effects, including university enrollment and employment. In addition to contributing to the global dialogue on the value of functional literacy, if the system demonstrates a positive impact on education and labor market outcomes, it may support the case for the cost-effectiveness and scalability of lighter touch, AI-based models in classrooms around the world.

title.narrative: Breathing for babies: revolutionizing care for acute respiratory distress

description.narrative: Acute respiratory distress is a common cause of death among the one million preterm babies worldwide who die every year. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is a proven effective therapy to reduce these deaths, but it is not available to the overwhelming majority of the worlds children, particularly in low-resource settings. Less than one percent of neonatal intensive care units surveyed across Africa reported being able to meet the oxygen blending (the combination of pure oxygen with air to regulate the concentration of oxygen delivered) needs of all their newborns. To increase the availability of CPAP where its needed most, Boston-based Vayu Global Health Innovations developed the Breathing for Babies packageincluding an innovative oxygen blender and a bubble CPAPthat do not require electricity or advanced bioengineering support, and that are available at one-third to one-half the cost of available alternatives. These Vayu devices have regulatory approval in Colombia, Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Brazil and emergency use authorization from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. To expand access to and scale Breathing for Babies, Vayu aims to generate awareness and demand through partnerships and demonstration programs. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, Vayu will conduct research to evaluate the effectiveness of the Breathing for Babies in different clinical settings, analyze its cost-effectiveness, implement demonstration programs in Ghana and Tanzania in close coordination with key stakeholders, and apply for additional country and global regulatory approvals. Given the current worldwide attention on the benefits of neonatal CPAP treatment, this evidence may help Vayu overcome regulatory hurdles and enable implementation through governments and international organizations.

title.narrative: HERA: Mobile Health Platform

description.narrative: As a free downloadable app, HERA leverages a digital health platform to increase the uptake of preventative health services for pregnant women and immunizations for children under two years of age. HERA application reduces demand-side barriers to accessing care by sending medical checkup and vaccination appointment reminders, centralizing medical records, and guiding users in navigating their local healthcare systems.

title.narrative: Scaling Sustainable Poverty Graduation in Rwanda

description.narrative: Village Enterprise developed a streamlined version of the poverty graduation model that has been rigorously tested and found to cost-effectively increase household consumption and assets for at least three and a half years. Village Enterprise will partner with the Government of Rwanda to implement a wide-scale pilot of its poverty graduation program with 22,000 Rwandan households and train government staff to lead the implementation of a pilot program with an additional 8,000 households. Village Enterprise and the Government of Rwanda will raise an additional $15 million to support the governments nationwide adoption and scale-up of a graduation program rooted in Village Enterprises approach, aiming to move more than one million Rwandans out of extreme poverty by 2026.

title.narrative: Inclusive Development and Equitable Assistance
Développement inclusif et assistance équitable

description.narrative: IDEA is a newaward which is designed to provide subgrants and capacity building to local organizations that focus on inclusive development, as well as implementing rapid responses to crises and opportunities related to ID Hub constituencies. It's also designed to be available for mission buy-in through field support, and of course has the option for associate awards to be created underneath the leader award, to specialize either in one country or region or one technical area related to inclusive development. it is intended strengthen programming and inclusive development by strengthening the capacity of local organizations headed by or representing marginalized and underrepresented groups and/or people in vulnerable situations as they advance their own development goals.

IDEA est un nouveau prix conçu pour fournir des subventions secondaires et un renforcement des capacités aux organisations locales qui se concentrent sur le développement inclusif, ainsi que pour la mise en œuvre de réponses rapides aux crises et aux opportunités liées aux circonscriptions d'ID Hub. Il est également conçu pour être disponible pour l'adhésion à la mission via le soutien sur le terrain, et offre bien sûr la possibilité de créer des récompenses d'associé sous la récompense de leader, pour se spécialiser soit dans un pays ou une région, soit dans un domaine technique lié au développement inclusif. il vise à renforcer la programmation et le développement inclusif en renforçant la capacité des organisations locales dirigées par ou représentant des groupes marginalisés et sous-représentés et/ou des personnes en situation vulnérable à mesure qu'elles progressent vers leurs propres objectifs de développement.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Irrigation and Mechanization Systems (ILIMS)
Nourrir le laboratoire d'innovation du futur pour les systèmes d'irrigation et de mécanisation (ILIMS)

description.narrative: ILIMS, led by the University of Nebraska's Daugherty Water for Food Global Insititute (DWFI) will gerneratre research-based evidence to support the growth of irrigation and mechanisation markets, develop strong insitutions and local capacity for sustainability, and foster opportunities for equitable access to services,information and technologies, especially among poor and women smallholders.

ILIMS, dirigé par le Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute (DWFI) de l'Université du Nebraska, générera des preuves fondées sur la recherche pour soutenir la croissance des marchés de l'irrigation et de la mécanisation, développer des institutions solides et des capacités locales de durabilité, et favoriser les opportunités d'accès équitable aux services, à l'information et aux technologies, en particulier parmi les petits exploitants pauvres et les femmes.

title.narrative: Farmer-to-Farmer (F2F) Program

description.narrative: The Farmer-to-Farmer (F2F) Program provides technical assistance from U.S. volunteers to farmers, farm groups, agribusinesses and other agriculture sector institutions in developing and transitional countries with the goal of promoting sustainable improvements in food security, agricultural processing, production, financing, and marketing. F2F leverages the expertise of volunteers from U.S. farms, universities, cooperatives, private agribusinesses and nonprofit farm organizations to respond to the local needs of host-country farmers and organizations. The program is aimed at reducing poverty and stimulating sustainable and broad-based economic growth.

description.narrative: (USAID Central America Regional): The Central America Service Corps (CASC)-Central America Youth Empowerment Program (CAYEP) MEL Platform provides coordination support for region-wide analysis, synthesis, and learning for activities that fall under the CASC initiative. The platform includes support for learning priorities and/or questions to guide the generation and use of evidence to better develop this regional initiative. This platform will provide MEL support specifically by developing and implementing a regional CASC learning agenda and MEL framework, providing primary and secondary data analysis and synthesis; and organizing and facilitating a community of practice.
Building Evidence for Decision-Making (BE4D) fournit à l'USAID et à ses partenaires des services MEL et CLA afin que les preuves soient utilisées pour la prise de décision.

title.narrative: Learning, Evaluation and Research III
Conception et apprentissage de programmes
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas

description.narrative: LER III is a global buy-in mechanism through the Evidence and Learning Office of the DRG Bureau, through which USAID Missions, Bureaus, and Independent Offices (M/B/IOs) can access research and evaluation services related to their DRG portfolios.

L'évaluation est la collecte et l'analyse systématiques d'informations sur les caractéristiques et les résultats des programmes et des projets comme base de jugement, pour améliorer l'efficacité et éclairer les décisions concernant la programmation actuelle et future. Les évaluations se distinguent de (a) les évaluations des besoins, qui sont conçues pour examiner le contexte du pays ou du secteur afin d'éclairer la conception du projet, (b) les examens informels internes des projets et (c) les audits (menés soit en interne, soit par un public externe). De tels efforts ne devraient pas être inclus dans le PO.3. Cependant, les évaluations d'évaluabilité -- les évaluations réalisées dans le but de déterminer si une évaluation d'une activité peut ou non être menée -- devraient être incluses dans l'OP.3. Ce domaine de programme devrait inclure toutes les évaluations conçues et financées grâce à l’aide étrangère, y compris les composants des contrats avec des ordres de tâches pour les évaluations (quel que soit le mécanisme). Il devrait également inclure tous les entrepreneurs indépendants embauchés uniquement pour produire une ou plusieurs évaluations ; tous les autres entrepreneurs (par exemple, ceux dont les responsabilités professionnelles peuvent inclure le soutien ou la gestion de l'évaluation mais pas la production d'une évaluation en tant que livrable) doivent être placés dans PO.2

La evaluación es la recopilación y el análisis sistemático de información sobre las características y resultados de programas y proyectos como base para emitir juicios, mejorar la eficacia e informar las decisiones sobre la programación actual y futura. Las evaluaciones son distintas de (a) evaluaciones de necesidades, que están diseñadas para examinar el contexto del país o del sector para informar el diseño de proyectos, (b) revisiones internas informales de proyectos y (c) auditorías (realizadas internamente o por una audiencia externa). Estos esfuerzos no deberían incluirse en el PO.3. Sin embargo, las evaluaciones de evaluabilidad (aquellas evaluaciones realizadas con el propósito de determinar si se puede realizar o no una evaluación de una actividad) deben incluirse en el PO.3. Esta área programática debe incluir todas las evaluaciones diseñadas y financiadas con fondos de asistencia extranjera, incluidos los componentes de los contratos con órdenes de trabajo para las evaluaciones (independientemente del mecanismo). También debe incluir a todos los contratistas independientes contratados únicamente para producir evaluaciones; todos los demás contratistas (por ejemplo, aquellos cuyas responsabilidades laborales pueden incluir el apoyo o la gestión de la evaluación pero no la producción de una evaluación como entregable) deben incluirse en el PO.2

title.narrative: Kenya Youth Professional Development
Faire progresser les résultats d’apprentissage en Afrique (ALOA)

description.narrative: (USAID Office of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (A/DEIA)): USAID will work in Kenya to support awards that increase employability and skills development for youth from marginalized communities. USAID will build a collaborative bridge between U.S.-based Historically Black Colleges and Universities, select Kenyan universities, and the private sector, including US-based companies. Partner universities will participate in capacity enriching activities such as exchanges, curriculum and course development, and research to help prepare a generation of innovative Kenyan leaders to meet evolving market demands. Private sector partners will amplify USG resources, providing input on practical skills, experiential learning experiences for university students, mentorship, shadowing opportunities and jobs. Partnerships will benefit US and Kenyan interests, advancing economic development specifically in the field of information and communication technologies and Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) education. .

Advancing Learning Outcomes for Africa (ALOA) est une initiative quinquennale de 65 millions de dollars financée par l’Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international (USAID) pour aider à concevoir, mettre en œuvre et évaluer des programmes d’éducation et de jeunesse en Afrique subsaharienne (ASS). Les objectifs de l'initiative comprennent : Support technique : fournir un soutien technique opportun et précis pour les progrès de l'éducation en Afrique. Renforcement des capacités : renforcer les capacités des missions et des organisations partenaires locales. Preuves et mesures : renforcer les preuves et les mesures.

title.narrative: The CIRCLE Alliance: Catalyzing Inclusive, Resilient, and Circular Local Economies" (CIRCLE Alliance)

description.narrative: The CIRCLE Alliance is USAID's flagship private sector partnership under the Agencys Save Our Seas Initiative. CIRCLE will create and accelerate local circular economies for plastics that improve livelihoods and reduce or divert a significant portion of recyclable waste currently entering the environment through three workstreams: reduce, reuse, recycle (3Rs) enterprise development, including piloting refill and reuse models; mandatory extended producer responsibility (EPR) policy development and implementation; and advancing gender equality and womens economic empowerment.

title.narrative: DRG: Democracy Indicators Monitoring Survey IV (DIMS 4)
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas

description.narrative: (USAID Latin America and Caribbean Regional): The Democracy Indicators Monitoring Survey IV (DIMS 4) will support public opinion survey research on democratic governance in 34 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) to measure citizens' engagement and promote evidence-driven discussions, policies, and programs. Using nationwide, randomized household surveys, DIMS4 addresses the absence of available independent, third party, longitudinal data, regarding public perception and lived experience on democracy in the LAC region. This data informs policy-making and program design. The AmericasBarometer, run from Vanderbilt University's LAPOP Lab, sets the gold standard for international surveys with unparalleled transparency, rigor and methodological innovation, data quality control, and inclusive tools for data dissemination and localized capacity-building..With FY 2024 funds, DIMS 4 will conduct a region-wide survey spanning 34 LAC countries. DIMS 4 conducts comparative, core studies in odd-numbered years (2023, 2025), and specialized studies in even-numbered years (2026, 2028). The comparative studies contain a common core module and country-specific questions, yet differ in emphasis. Specialized surveys may focus on intentions to migrate, or perception of human rights. Surveys will be conducted face-to-face unless circumstances require randomized phone surveys. .DIMS4 supports US policy priorities and Mission objectives including: The Root Causes Strategy and the WHA-LAC Bureau Joint Regional Strategy Objective 3.1: Restore and strengthen democratic governance at all levels, and across sectors and program areas. DIMS4 aligns with USAID's Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment Policy goals by ensuring an adequate supply of public perception data, to include as relevant gender-related questions. DIMS4 supports Mission objectives to strengthen democracy, which flows from the Joint Strategic Plan 2022-2026.

Esta área del programa cubre componentes de diseño de programas y gestión del desempeño y aprendizaje. Esta área apoya la evaluación, los estudios y análisis especiales, la planificación estratégica, el diseño de programas y proyectos, el seguimiento de programas (para incluir estudios de referencia y otras necesidades de recopilación de datos) y actividades que apoyan el aprendizaje, la transferencia de conocimientos y la adaptación de proyectos. La evaluación incluye el examen del estado de un contexto nacional o sectorial para informar el diseño del proyecto, pero no incluye la evaluación de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos (consulte el Área programática PO.3 para obtener una definición de evaluación). Estudios o análisis especiales podrían respaldar la planificación estratégica o de proyectos o incluir investigaciones para el aprendizaje general que no esté necesariamente relacionado con el desempeño de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esta área programática también puede incluir la preparación de planes estratégicos y otras tareas de programación a corto plazo, la evaluación del potencial de las tecnologías de la información y las comunicaciones para mejorar el desempeño a lo largo del ciclo del programa o la difusión de mejores prácticas y lecciones aprendidas.

title.narrative: Evaluating Progressive Versus Proportional Digitized Property Tax Collection

description.narrative: Low tax revenue is a significant challenge facing governments in low-income countries, which typically collect less than half of the revenue that high-income countries collect as a share of gross domestic product. Without enough revenue, governments cannot provide the public goods and services necessary for economic development. To examine whether progressive property taxation can increase tax compliance and revenues in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), which collected just 9 percent of its GDP in 2021, the implementing partner is partnering with a provincial tax authority on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) that compares neighborhoods that are assigned to the current flat fee schedule, a proportional tax rate schedule, or a schedule of progressive property tax rates. The participating neighborhoods are in the provincial capital of Karanga. This RCT measures the effects of the different tax schedules on total government revenue, household compliance, perceptions of fairness, and motivation to pay taxes and is designed to inform future tax policy. This contract will increase the endline survey sample to improve the studys ability to detect statistically significant effects. This funding will also help scale up digitization of the tax assessment process. Digitization, including the development of a comprehensive database of properties and assessed values, will strengthen the provincial governments ability to administer taxes by improving record keeping and updating.

description.narrative: Despite generating approximately 15 percent of Mexicos gross domestic product, neighborhood corner storeswhere many people purchase grocery and household productsoften lack access to the capital they need to purchase enough inventory to grow their businesses. To make capital available to neighborhood retailers, the implementing partner has partnered with some of the largest companies that distribute the fast-moving consumer goods sold in neighborhood stores and developed a buy now, pay later (BNPL) tool that plugs into the purchase portal of these distributor partners. Using a proprietary algorithm, the implementing partner identifies creditworthy retailers to receive a short-term loan offer when they check out with their distributor. If the offer is accepted, retailers register via WhatsApp, the implementing partner pays the distributor to deliver the stock, and retailers have 15 days to repay with interest or be assessed a modest late fee. This activity will conduct a randomized controlled trial to understand the impact of the platform on the revenues and household income of participating retailers and to test varying interest rates and late fees to determine optimal contract terms. In addition, the implementing partner aims to expand eligibility to higher-risk retailers. Overall, the implementing partner will use grant funds to reach more retailers, which is expected to attract capital and debt investment to sustainably grow.

title.narrative: ARCED Foundation: Aureolin Research, Consultancy, and Expertise Development: Using Satellite Imagery to Reduce Air Pollution

description.narrative: In Bangladesh, air pollution shortens the average person's life by 6.9 years. The country's average annual particulate concentration is almost 74, nearly 15 times the WHO guideline of five. Exposure to air pollution causes life-threatening diseases such as asthma, cancer, and heart disease. In 2014, the Government of Bangladesh introduced a regulation that makes a primary source of pollutants brick kilns illegal near population centers, schools, and medical facilities. However, kilns continue to operate in violation of the regulation due to insufficient enforcement, putting the health of millions of people at risk. In 2022, Bangladesh's Department of the Environment (DoE) found that 60 percent of the country's 7,881 brick kilns operate illegally without environmental clearance and that up to 58 percent of fine particles (commonly referred to as PM2.5) in Dhaka air come from brick kilns. To increase the efficiency of limited enforcement resources, the ARCED Foundation (ARCED) developed an information system that combines satellite images with machine learning algorithms to identify and locate brick kilns and predict the health harm each individual kiln causes based on proximity to schools, healthcare facilities, and population centers. ARCED packaged this information in a user-friendly dashboard, which the DoE is already actively using to prioritize brick kiln regulations to minimize negative health effects. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, ARCED will conduct a randomized controlled trial to determine whether the system improves the efficiency of enforcement action and ultimately reduces the number of harmful kilns in operation. If the trial is successful, ARCED will transfer the technology to the DoE and train government employees to update and maintain the system. ARCED's system has the potential to benefit Bangladesh's entire population of 170 million people, growing its positive impact over time as more kiln operators are deterred from operating

title.narrative: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Consumer Overdraft for Financial Resilience

description.narrative: FINCA International is partnering with Kuunda, a business-to-business financial technology solutions provider that has developed a menu of affordable, real-time overdraft solutions for last mile consumers and mobile money agents. Kuundas consumer overdraft product provides instant microloans using an algorithm that leverages consumer transactional data to generate credit scores. DIV will support FINCA and Kuunda by funding a randomized controlled trial of the consumer overdraft product in Tanzania. The study will measure the impact of the overdraft product on indicators of household and financial wellbeing, including consumption, business expenditures, and ability to manage financial shocks. In addition, Kuunda will test if it can continue to sustainably scale its model while lowering its credit score threshold and extending overdraft protection to more consumers.

title.narrative: Testing Community-Led Outreach Clinics to Improve Health in Rural Areas

description.narrative: Access to high quality healthcare is a critical driver of human capital and a cornerstone of broader individual and societal well-being. In Uganda, rural access to health care and to essential medicines remains a persistent challenge; although 86% of Ugandans live in rural areas, only 15-20% of the countrys doctors work in those same areas, which contributes to poorer health outcomes among rural populations. Aside from a few irregular, one-day mobile clinics or sponsored medical missions, there are few resources in place for delivering healthcare on a regular basis to people in remote areas. We partnered with Health Access Connect (HAC), a Ugandan-based NGO that coordinates monthly, financially self-sustainable outreach visits by clinical staff from government health facilities to rural communities that are located at least 5 km away from public health facilities. Through a cluster-randomized trial in 64 health facilities and 128 villages, this study will evaluate the impact of HACs community-based outreach activities on the demand, quality, and utilization of health services, household health outcomes, child schooling and human capital, and household labor market incomes.

title.narrative: Experimental Evidence on Public-Private Partnerships in Education
Productividad del Sector Privado

description.narrative: In many developing countries, particularly in rapidly urbanizing cities, families in low-income neighborhoods lack access to high-quality education. In Bogot, Colombia, a major problem identified in the 1990s was that many of the poorest children in the city were not attending school; and, of those that were, nearly one third were enrolled in private, unsubsidized schools of variable and usually low quality. To address this, Bogot introduced a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model in the early 2000s, which authorized private schools to bid on public contracts to operate in underserved areas. These schools, known as Concession Schools or Schools in Administration (SA), are given autonomy in pedagogy design but are held accountable to universal academic and administrative performance standards. A prior quasi-experimental study found that SA schools improved students cognitive performance and socioemotional outcomes, and that operating costs and student drop-out rates were lower, compared to public schools. To provide more rigorous evidence on the SA school model, Vanderbilt University and Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) Colombia in collaboration with the Secretary of Education of Bogota began a randomized controlled trial (RCT) in 2021 to determine the impact of being offered enrollment via the SA schools admissions lottery on students academic and socioemotional outcomes. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, the research team will expand the RCT to include an additional student cohort, extend the follow-up period to measure longer-term impacts on students outcomes, and analyze SA schools cost-effectiveness.

title.narrative: Piloting Digital Training for Lay First Responders

description.narrative: Road traffic injuries are a leading cause of death globally, particularly affecting low and middle-income countries where emergency medical services (EMS) may be scarce. EMS reaches less than 10 percent of sub-Saharan Africans, a critical gap in access to prehospital healthcare; this need is especially acute in countries like Sierra Leone, which does not have EMS. LFR International developed the Lay First Responder (LFR) model to address this gap by training lay people who are frequently on the roadssuch as motorcycle taxi driversto administer prehospital care, given their proximity to injury, wide self-dispersion in search of customers, and possession of a means of patient transportation. After qualifying through a short in-person training program, lay first responders can respond quickly to accidents, providing emergency trauma care and transportation to medical facilities. A previously-conducted pre-post study suggests the model improves trainees emergency care knowledge and skills while significantly expanding access to emergency care for the community. LFR seeks to convert its training curriculum to a digital program on a mobile application, which can more cost-effectively reach trainees by providing a digital approach to scale its training in resource-limited settings. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, LFR International will conduct a small-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate the effectiveness of digital versus in-person training on lay first responders knowledge and skills retention. The study also seeks to identify the qualities that lead an individual to be a super responder, i.e., individuals who were identified in a prior study as more likely to respond to incidents. If successful, the RCT results could validate the scalability of the LFR model, making it attractive to public sector partnerships and leading to broader adoption across West Africa, cost-effectively addressing a critical public health challe

title.narrative: Evaluating the Impact of Rainwater Harvesting Technology at Scale

description.narrative: In Niger, 250,000 hectares of land are lost every year to desertification. This drastic loss of productive land harms smallholder farmers who depend on fertile soil for food and livelihoods. To help restore the degraded soil, researchers are testing a rainwater harvesting method built around two catchment techniques that collect both rainfall and runoff while increasing the nutrient content of the soil: demi-lunes (half-moons) and zai (soil pits). After a simple training, farmers are able to construct the catchments themselves using a pickaxe and a shovel, which they likely already own. The team previously conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to evaluate approaches to trainings on demi-lune construction and found that the trainings increased adoption of the technique from 4 percent in the control group to 95 percent in the training group in the first year and resulted in a meaningful (0.15 standard deviation) increase in agricultural production over three years. However, few smallholder farmers know how to construct demi-lunes and zais. Building upon the results of the previous, the researchers are conducting a new RCT in partnership with the Government of Niger and Sahel Consulting Group to: (1) optimize the rainwater harvesting training program so that it can be administered sustainably by the government and other partners in Niger and (2) evaluate the effectiveness of the program at scale. In addition, the research will compare the costs and benefits of in-person monitoring with remote sensing techniques. Results from these studies will inform the Government of Nigers efforts to promote rainwater harvesting as a defense against desertification as it aims to preserve the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers.

title.narrative: Testing a Behavior Change Approach to Counter Criminal Youth Recruitment
Productividad del Sector Privado

description.narrative: Each year, roughly one million children across Latin America are recruited into organized crime, contributing to a region-wide crisis of gang violence. Gangs are responsible for half of the homicides in the region, and their presence impacts urban communities in numerous ways, from reducing perceptions of safety to stifling investment. In Colombia, gang recruitment has escalated in recent years, including in Medelln. The Parceritos program is a cognitive behavioral intervention that seeks to address gang recruitment in Medelln. The program combines behavioral change techniques with information on the economic and social benefits from education to shift high-risk adolescent boys toward more productive futures. The approach is informed by growing evidence that cognitive behavioral interventions can reduce criminality, as well as two years of targeted interviews with over 8,500 teenage boys in Colombia, and a successful small-scale pilot. Funding from this contract will support a randomized controlled trial to rigorously evaluate the Parceritos programs impact on gang membership and engagement with the criminal justice system, as well as school completion, occupational choice, and earnings. This contract will also support the dissemination of results and preparation to scale to other urban areas should the evaluation find positive results. If Parceritos proves successful, it could help to prevent youth involvement in organized crime in Latin America and beyond.

title.narrative: AI-based Entrepreneurship Training Pilot
Productividad del Sector Privado

description.narrative: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) represent about 90 percent of businesses worldwide and generate a significant portion of jobs and economic output, especially in developing countries. Research has shown that certain business and management practices are associated with higher rates of enterprise survival and sales growth. Governments and donors spend significant resources to provide training to help entrepreneurs implement these practices. While such training can be effective, it is often also intensive and expensive, and therefore limited in scale. Leveraging recent advances in large language models, Hacer Peru has developed a training, mentoring, and consulting tool called MAIA that aims to provide guidance on leading business and management practices to small business owners at a fraction of the cost. Delivered via WhatsApp, MAIA draws on information specific to the needs of MSMEs in Peru and responds in real-time to questions and challenges faced by entrepreneurs. With the support of Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), Hacer Peru will build on an initial pilot of the MAIA platform to reach 4,000 bodegueros (convenience store owners) and expand into a second sector. Hacer Peru will conduct testing, such as changing the models emphasis and the frequency and type of notifications, to determine the best ways to encourage engagement and learning among entrepreneurs. Hacer Peru will also use the DIV award to develop additional modules to make the platform more useful for various industries. The steps taken by Hacer Peru could help identify a substantially more affordable way to deliver entrepreneurship training and consulting services to MSMEs in Peru and around the world.

title.narrative: Testing Unite for a Better Life, a Program to Reduce Intimate Partner Violence
Productivité du secteur privé

description.narrative: To help reduce intimate partner violence (IPV), the Paris School of Economics (PSE) seeks to test two adaptations of an IPV prevention program, Unite for a Better Life (UBL), in Cameroon. UBL has previously been piloted and tested in Ethiopia. The program aims to reduce IPV by addressing social norms and behaviors through structured, culturally relevant sessions that include discussion, activities, and exercises led by trained facilitators. In Cameroon, the sessions and program delivery have been adjusted to incorporate lessons from the Ethiopia trial and will be delivered via two methods. The in-person delivery approach differs from previous program iterations by engaging couples in sessions that are held separately for men and women, while a podcast adaptation aims to offer a scalable, technology-based approach. With support from DIV, PSE, in collaboration with a local non-profit, Leap Girl, and the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), will conduct a cluster randomized controlled trial to evaluate UBL as delivered in-person and via podcasts in Cameroon. The study will evaluate UBLs impact on IPV in the 18 months after implementation, as well as womens perceptions of changes in their male partners behavior and shifts in gender norms. By generating rigorous evidence on the effectiveness of UBL as delivered via these two methods, results from this study are designed to contribute to global efforts to address IPV and improve the well-being of women in fragile settings.

title.narrative: Evaluating a Motivational Video to Inspire Math Achievement at Scale

description.narrative: Despite their potential for impactful careers in science and technology, disadvantaged students often lack exposure to STEM opportunities and are under-represented in STEM education and careers. This lack of representation limits both individual potential and broader economic growth. In Brazil, the national Math Olympiad competition offers an opportunity to bridge this gap. Studies have found that participation in the Olympiadwhich is open to all schools across the countryboosts math scores on standardized exams and increases the likelihood of enrollment in selective universities. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, The Agency Fund will evaluate the impact of a 30-minute inspirational video designed to motivate underrepresented students to continue participating in the Olympiad and to pursue studies in STEM fields and careers. This intervention targets the top 5 percent of students selected for the second round of the competition and aims to inspire students to change their beliefs and aspirations about their own abilities. Without this motivational intervention, many talented students may self-select out of STEM opportunities. Researchers will conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) involving 12,000 schools, where students in the treatment arm will be exposed to the video. Outcomes will include Math Olympiad performance, national standardized exam scores, and university enrollment, as well as changes in student beliefs about STEM. DIV will support key activities including formative research, video production, iterative testing of the video, and RCT implementation. If the video intervention proves effective, it could be scaled across Brazil at a minimal cost through the Brazilian Math Olympiad organization, helping to increase diversity and close gaps in STEM education and careers.

title.narrative: Evaluating a Social Protection Program to Reduce Poverty

description.narrative: The Government of Indonesia has begun piloting PENA (Economic Heroes), a social protection program inspired by the evidence-based Graduation Approach. The Graduation Approach centers on a larger one-time asset transfer and accompanying support, such as counseling, to help move households out of poverty. However, additional innovation is needed to adapt elements of the graduation approach to the Indonesian context and facilitate implementation on a massive scale. With DIV support, Harvard researchers will innovate and test PENAs design, including streamlining it for scalability. Along with partners, they will conduct a randomized controlled trial to rigorously evaluate several variations of PENA to understand: (1) whether it is more effective at improving key outcomes than current social assistance programs; (2) how to identify people who have the highest potential to graduate from social assistance programs; (3) which program variations are most effective; and (4) whether such programs can be made easier to scale without compromising effectiveness.

title.narrative: Adapting a Therapy Approach to Prevent Crime

description.narrative: Urban crime and violence pose significant challenges around the world. Young men, in particular, are at a higher risk of engaging in criminal activitieswith a high proportion of crimes often committed by a relatively small number of young men. Unlike traditional approaches to crime that focus on punitive measures and policing, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a proactive, targeted, evidence-based, and cost-effective approach for changing behavior. CBT programs have been shown to reduce criminal activity by helping individuals improve coping mechanisms, impulse control, and decision-making skills. The partner started implementing the CBT-driven Sustainable Transformation of Youth in Liberia (STYL) program in 2012. A randomized controlled trial found that STYLs approach (targeted CBT plus a cash transfer) significantly reduced high-risk mens likelihood of committing crimes and engaging in antisocial behaviors, including a 40 percent reduction in engagement in theft and robbery in the first year after the programs completion. A follow-up study found that these effects were sustained ten years later; for example, the program cut participants' likelihood of committing theft or robbery in half. This grant will test and scale the STYL program in Nigeria. The implementing partner will pilot STYL with high-risk young men in Lagos to assess the applicability of STYL to other contexts and will test adaptation strategies for scalability while working to ensure implementation fidelity of the STYL program as it scales.

title.narrative: Scaling Government-led Graduation Programs to Alleviate Poverty

description.narrative: BRAC pioneered the Graduation Approach to address the complex nature of extreme poverty. It consists of a set of core interventions designed to enable households to overcome the various challenges of extreme poverty and generate sustained improvements in their income, consumption, and overall well-being. With support from DIV, BRAC will work with the governments of Indonesia and the Philippines to integrate the Graduation Approachs core interventions into current poverty reduction strategies, programs, and budgets. This award will also support independent research on key design and implementation processes, as well as qualitative research to establish the most effective pathways to scale through governments. Ultimately, BRAC aims to enable the governments of Indonesia and the Philippines to deliver high-quality Graduation programming to 30,000 households within the award period, and to millions more over the next decade.

title.narrative: Environmental Support Services Contract (ESSE II)
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas
Diseño y aprendizaje de programas
Design e aprendizagem do programa

description.narrative: The activity will directly enhance the ENVE team's ability to provide mission support across multiple technical areas

Esta área del programa cubre componentes de diseño de programas y gestión del desempeño y aprendizaje. Esta área apoya la evaluación, los estudios y análisis especiales, la planificación estratégica, el diseño de programas y proyectos, el seguimiento de programas (para incluir estudios de referencia y otras necesidades de recopilación de datos) y actividades que apoyan el aprendizaje, la transferencia de conocimientos y la adaptación de proyectos. La evaluación incluye el examen del estado de un contexto nacional o sectorial para informar el diseño del proyecto, pero no incluye la evaluación de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos (consulte el Área programática PO.3 para obtener una definición de evaluación). Estudios o análisis especiales podrían respaldar la planificación estratégica o de proyectos o incluir investigaciones para el aprendizaje general que no esté necesariamente relacionado con el desempeño de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esta área programática también puede incluir la preparación de planes estratégicos y otras tareas de programación a corto plazo, la evaluación del potencial de las tecnologías de la información y las comunicaciones para mejorar el desempeño a lo largo del ciclo del programa o la difusión de mejores prácticas y lecciones aprendidas.

La evaluación incluye el examen del estado de un contexto nacional o sectorial para informar el diseño del proyecto, pero no incluye la evaluación de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos (consulte el Área programática PO.3 para obtener una definición de evaluación). Estudios o análisis especiales podrían respaldar la planificación estratégica o de proyectos o incluir investigaciones para el aprendizaje general que no esté necesariamente relacionado con el desempeño de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esta área programática también puede incluir la preparación de planes estratégicos y otras tareas de programación a corto plazo, la evaluación del potencial de las tecnologías de la información y las comunicaciones para mejorar el desempeño a lo largo del ciclo del programa o la difusión de mejores prácticas y lecciones aprendidas.

Esta área programática cobre componentes de concepção de programas e gestão de desempenho e aprendizagem. Esta área apoia a avaliação, estudos e análises especiais, planeamento estratégico, concepção de programas e projectos, monitorização de programas (para incluir estudos de base e outras necessidades de recolha de dados) e actividades que apoiam a aprendizagem, transferência de conhecimentos e adaptação de projectos. A avaliação inclui o exame do estado de um país ou contexto sectorial para informar a concepção do projecto, mas não inclui a avaliação das actividades financiadas pelo Governo dos EUA (ver Área Programática PO.3 para uma definição de avaliação). Estudos ou análises especiais poderiam apoiar o planeamento estratégico ou de projectos ou incluir investigação para aprendizagem geral que não esteja necessariamente relacionada com o desempenho de actividades financiadas pelo Governo dos EUA. Esta área programática também pode incluir a preparação de planos estratégicos e outras tarefas de programação de curto prazo, a avaliação do potencial das tecnologias de informação e comunicação para melhorar o desempenho ao longo do ciclo do programa ou a divulgação de melhores práticas e lições aprendidas.

title.narrative: Demographic and Health Surveys - 9 (DHS-9)

description.narrative: The DHS Program works with governments to collect and share key information about people, their health and their health systems. This includes information on infant and child mortality, fertility, family planning use, maternal health, child immunization, malnutrition levels, HIV prevalence, and malaria. Anyone can access the data from these surveys, and the indicators are comparable over time and across countries. Governments, donors, researchers, and civil society (such as faith-based organizations and other domestic and international organizations) use the information from these surveys to inform health-related programming, policies, funding priorities, and research.

Le programme DHS travaille avec les gouvernements pour collecter et partager des informations clés sur les personnes, leur santé et leurs systèmes de santé. Cela comprend des informations sur la mortalité infantile et juvénile, la fécondité, le recours à la planification familiale, la santé maternelle, la vaccination des enfants, les niveaux de malnutrition, la prévalence du VIH et le paludisme. Tout le monde peut accéder aux données de ces enquêtes, et les indicateurs sont comparables dans le temps et entre les pays. Les gouvernements, les donateurs, les chercheurs et la société civile (telles que les organisations confessionnelles et autres organisations nationales et internationales) utilisent les informations de ces enquêtes pour éclairer les programmes, les politiques, les priorités de financement et la recherche liés à la santé.

description.narrative: This program supports the Mission's goal for an independent, prosperous, and healthy Ukraine united around core European values in one or more of the following sectors: strengthening of democratic governance, and more inclusive, sustainable, market-driven economic growth.

title.narrative: The 2021-2025 Strategy (GAVI 5.0)

description.narrative: The 2021-2025 strategy (GAVI 5.0), which was approved by the GAVI board in june 2019, builds on the alliances years of demonstrated success and strives toward its vision to leave no one behind with immunization. to increase coverage and equity, GAVI 5.0 prioritizes zero-dose children who have not received a single vaccine shot as well as missed communities. the zero-dose agenda is also a key priority for the global communitys immunization agenda 2030, which was endorsed by the world health assembly in may 2020.

title.narrative: Global Financing Facility

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): The GFF contribution will enhance country and global efforts to create resilient, epidemic-ready, and sustainably financed primary health care systems and health workforces that are capable of responding during health emergencies arising from emerging infectious disease threats. COVID-19, Ebola, and other major outbreaks have illustrated that infectious disease threats can overwhelm fragile primary health care systems and disrupt routine prevention and treatment services with disastrous implications. Strong primary health care systems are also the prerequisite for establishing the community-based surveillance needed to detect new infectious disease threats, delivering rapid frontline responses, and providing outbreak and pandemic response services throughout the duration of the health emergency. This funding, through a direct agreement with the World Bank, will provide technical assistance to governments to strengthen resilient, epidemic-ready primary health care systems that are capable of effectively delivering outbreak and pandemic response services. It will strengthen the ability of governments to support routine health information systems and rapid assessments to track disruptions in services due to pandemics or other emerging health threats, and more rapidly respond based on near-real-time signals.

description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): The Census InterAgency Agreement's overall purpose is to support countries to produce and disseminate accurate, relevant, and timely population statistics for development. It is design to achieve four key results: 1) improved tools, methods, and resources for census, survey, administrative and other data collection, analysis, and use; 2) improved capacity of individuals and organizations to collect, analyze, disseminate and use high-quality data in a timely fashion; 3) increased availability and use of timely and relevant geospatial and population-based data; and 4) coordination and leadership within the international community in building more robust data ecosystems in resource-constrained environments. Anticipated longer-term outcomes include enhanced quantity, quality, and use of population data for policy development, development and humanitarian assistance planning, program formulation, and monitoring and evaluation, and increased sustainable country capacity to collect and utilize population data. Key topics of focus under this IAA include strengthening national statistical systems to improve country data, integrating georeferenced data to deepen analysis and insights, and improving geospatial modeling of vulnerable populations in collaboration with USAID's GeoCenter on activities that support USAID's Geospatial Strategy.

Ce domaine de programme couvre les composantes de la conception des programmes, de la gestion des performances et de l'apprentissage. Ce domaine prend en charge l'évaluation, les études et analyses spéciales, la planification stratégique, la conception de programmes et de projets, le suivi des programmes (pour inclure les études de base et autres besoins de collecte de données) et les activités qui soutiennent l'apprentissage, le transfert de connaissances et l'adaptation des projets. L'évaluation comprend l'examen de l'état d'un pays ou d'un contexte sectoriel pour éclairer la conception du projet, mais n'inclut pas l'évaluation des activités financées par le gouvernement américain (veuillez consulter le domaine de programme PO.3 pour une définition de l'évaluation). Des études ou analyses spéciales pourraient soutenir la planification stratégique ou de projet ou inclure des recherches pour un apprentissage général qui n'est pas nécessairement lié à la performance des activités financées par le gouvernement américain. Ce domaine de programme peut également inclure la préparation de plans stratégiques et d'autres tâches de programmation à court terme, l'évaluation du potentiel des technologies de l'information et de la communication pour améliorer les performances tout au long du cycle du programme ou la diffusion des meilleures pratiques et des enseignements tirés.

Esta área del programa cubre componentes de diseño de programas y gestión del desempeño y aprendizaje. Esta área apoya la evaluación, los estudios y análisis especiales, la planificación estratégica, el diseño de programas y proyectos, el seguimiento de programas (para incluir estudios de referencia y otras necesidades de recopilación de datos) y actividades que apoyan el aprendizaje, la transferencia de conocimientos y la adaptación de proyectos. La evaluación incluye el examen del estado de un contexto nacional o sectorial para informar el diseño del proyecto, pero no incluye la evaluación de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos (consulte el Área programática PO.3 para obtener una definición de evaluación). Estudios o análisis especiales podrían respaldar la planificación estratégica o de proyectos o incluir investigaciones para el aprendizaje general que no esté necesariamente relacionado con el desempeño de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esta área programática también puede incluir la preparación de planes estratégicos y otras tareas de programación a corto plazo, la evaluación del potencial de las tecnologías de la información y las comunicaciones para mejorar el desempeño a lo largo del ciclo del programa o la difusión de mejores prácticas y lecciones aprendidas.

title.narrative: Evaluation

description.narrative: Evaluation is the systematic collection and analysis of information about the characteristics and outcomes of programs and projects as a basis for judgments, to improve effectiveness and inform decisions about current and future programming. Evaluations are distinct from (a) needs assessments, which are designed to examine country or sector context to inform project design, (b) internal informal reviews of projects and (c) audits (conducted either internally or by an external audience). Such efforts should not be included in PO.3. However, evaluability assessments -- those assessments completed with the purpose of determining whether or not an evaluation of an activity can be conducted -- should be included in PO.3. This program area should include all evaluations designed and funded with foreign assistance funding, including the components of contracts with task orders for evaluations (regardless of the mechanism). It should also include all independent contractors hired solely to produce an evaluation(s); all other contractors (e.g., those whose job responsibilities may include support or management of evaluation but not the production of an evaluation as a deliverable) should be placed in PO.2

title.narrative: Regional Water and Vulnerable Environment (WAVE) Activity: Environmental Restoration of the Aral Sea (ERAS)

description.narrative: Regional Water and Vulnerable Environment (WAVE) Activity: Environmental Restoration of the Aral Sea (ERAS): At the request of the Government of Kazakhstan, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) has launched the Environmental Restoration of the Aral Sea I (ERAS-I) Activity. The goal of the activity is to provide environmental restoration measures to improve the resilience of landscapes in the Northern Aral Sea zone. The implementation of the Environmental Restoration of the Aral Sea I Activity supports regional transboundary cooperation for water and environment and enhances resilience to climate change for vulnerable populations and ecosystems. The Environmental Restoration of the Aral Sea I Activity aims to introduce innovative measures to create an Oasis using black saxaul in the Northern Aral Sea zone, 50 km from the village of Karateren. The innovative methods which include a research design to assess the optimal growth conditions for soil and watering will create a stable ecological system with endemic species of flora and fauna.

title.narrative: Kazakhstan Rule of Law Program

description.narrative: (Kazakhstan): The Kazakhstan Rule of Law activity (KROL) strengthens the independence of the judiciary and creates a favorable legal environment for businesses and civil society organizations (CSOs). The objectives of the activity include: (1) strengthening the investment climate and business enabling environment, (2) improving the legal enabling environment for nonprofit organizations and (3) increasing independence and professionalism of the judiciary. The program's focus on implementation of the newly adopted Administrative Procedure and Process Code was designed to allow businesses and investors to understand that the Courts could serve as a check on agency decisions that were otherwise unpredictable and lacked the appearance of impartiality. USAID will support improvements to the administrative procedural code by introducing presumption of innocence best practices. Partnering with the Union of Judges, the activity plans to improve the Judicial Code of Ethics. The activity also plans to work with the Ministry of Information and Social Development to create a new Law on Non-Commercial Organizations and provide online courses for legislation drafting to align this process with international standards to make the lawmaking process more transparent and participatory. USAID will support efforts to build the Government-CSOs partnership to further promote transparency and accountability.This activity contributes to the U.S.Integrated Country Strategy Objective 2.2: Democratic institutions and human rights protections are enhanced by advancing civil liberties and rule of law, and demonstrating political will to conduct objective, transparent investigations into allegations of official misconduct; and U.S. Strategy for Central Asia Objective 5: Promote rule of law reform and respect for human rights and Objective 6: Promote US investment in and development of Central Asia; CAATSA Goal 2: Anti-corruption and rule of law and Goal 5: independent media and civil society.

title.narrative: USAID Power Central Asia Activity Phase I

description.narrative: USAIDs Power Central Asia will assist national governments, utilities, and other stakeholders to develop domestic energy market reforms, help strengthen the regional electricity market, and promote greater adoption of clean energy technologies from conventional and renewable sources. The program will assist Central Asian countries to balance hydropower generation needs with other water management priorities. USAID will also help to ensure the safe management of sensitive data generated during the program.

title.narrative: Program Design and Learning

description.narrative: Evaluation is the systematic collection and analysis of information about the characteristics and outcomes of programs and projects as a basis for judgments, to improve effectiveness and inform decisions about current and future programming. Evaluations are distinct from (a) needs assessments, which are designed to examine country or sector context to inform project design, (b) internal informal reviews of projects and (c) audits (conducted either internally or by an external audience). Such efforts should not be included in PO.3. However, evaluability assessments -- those assessments completed with the purpose of determining whether or not an evaluation of an activity can be conducted -- should be included in PO.3. This program area should include all evaluations designed and funded with foreign assistance funding, including the components of contracts with task orders for evaluations (regardless of the mechanism). It should also include all independent contractors hired solely to produce an evaluation(s); all other contractors (e.g., those whose job responsibilities may include support or management of evaluation but not the production of an evaluation as a deliverable) should be placed in PO.2

title.narrative: Countering Violent Extremism in Central Asia Activity

description.narrative: (Central Asia Regional): The Regional Countering Violent Extremism in Central Asia (CVECA) Activity will build upon the successes of the recent Central Asia Support for Stable Societies activity and the findings from its research and pilot programs. The new activity will support the C5+1 platform and will work in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan to reduce the risk of recruitment into, and support for, violent extremism (VE); and build the capacity and commitment of our partners to prevent and counter the VE threats they face. USAID/Central Asia aims to strengthen resilience to VE across the countries of Central Asia with a portfolio of interventions over five years that advance several interrelated objectives, including strengthening the capacity of local-level community leaders-particularly women-and CSOs; helping at-risk individuals and families to enhance their skills and strengthen their support networks; increasing social cohesion in at-risk communities and fostering opportunities to form positive relationships with vulnerable individuals and reduce marginalization. This activity supports the U.S. Strategy for Central Asia objective 1: Support and Strengthen the Sovereignty and Independence of the Central Asian States, Individually and as a Region; and Objective 2: Reduce terrorist threats in Central Asia. The activity also supports CAATSA Objective 2: Rule of Law. This activity supports Countering Violent Extremism key issues.

title.narrative: Program Design and Learning

description.narrative: This program area covers components of program design and performance management and learning. This area supports assessment, special studies and analysis, strategic planning, program and project design, program monitoring (to include baseline studies and other data collection needs) and activities that support learning, knowledge transfer and adaptation of projects. Assessment includes the examination of the state of a country or sector context to inform project design but does not include evaluation of USG-funded activities (please see Program Area PO.3 for a definition of evaluation). Special studies or analysis could support strategic or project planning or include research for general learning that is not necessarily related to the performance of USG-funded activities. This program area may also include the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks, assessment of the potential of information and communication technologies to enhance performance throughout the program cycle or dissemination of best practices and lessons learned.

title.narrative: Evaluation

description.narrative: Evaluation is the systematic collection and analysis of information about the characteristics and outcomes of programs and projects as a basis for judgments, to improve effectiveness and inform decisions about current and future programming. Evaluations are distinct from (a) needs assessments, which are designed to examine country or sector context to inform project design, (b) internal informal reviews of projects and (c) audits (conducted either internally or by an external audience). Such efforts should not be included in PO.3. However, evaluability assessments -- those assessments completed with the purpose of determining whether or not an evaluation of an activity can be conducted -- should be included in PO.3. This program area should include all evaluations designed and funded with foreign assistance funding, including the components of contracts with task orders for evaluations (regardless of the mechanism). It should also include all independent contractors hired solely to produce an evaluation(s); all other contractors (e.g., those whose job responsibilities may include support or management of evaluation but not the production of an evaluation as a deliverable) should be placed in PO.2

title.narrative: Program Design and Learning

description.narrative: This program area covers components of program design and performance management and learning. This area supports assessment, special studies and analysis, strategic planning, program and project design, program monitoring (to include baseline studies and other data collection needs) and activities that support learning, knowledge transfer and adaptation of projects. Assessment includes the examination of the state of a country or sector context to inform project design but does not include evaluation of USG-funded activities (please see Program Area PO.3 for a definition of evaluation). Special studies or analysis could support strategic or project planning or include research for general learning that is not necessarily related to the performance of USG-funded activities. This program area may also include the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks, assessment of the potential of information and communication technologies to enhance performance throughout the program cycle or dissemination of best practices and lessons learned.

title.narrative: USAID/Kosovo Local Works Activity

description.narrative: The purpose of the Local Works Activity is to increase socio-economic cohesion among target communitiesKosovo Roma, Ashkali, and Egyptianthrough the facilitation of sustainable recycling models led by the private sector and in cooperation with communities and local governments. For the purpose of this activity the target stakeholder communities can be defined broadly as marginalized groups (Roma, Ashkali, and Egyptian communities, youth, women and girls)

description.narrative: This program supports the Mission's goal for an independent, prosperous, and healthy Ukraine united around core European values in one or more of the following sectors: strengthening of democratic governance, and more inclusive, sustainable, market-driven economic growth.

Ce programme soutient l'objectif de la mission d'une Ukraine indépendante, prospère et saine, unie autour des valeurs européennes fondamentales dans un ou plusieurs des secteurs suivants : le renforcement de la gouvernance démocratique et une croissance économique plus inclusive, durable et axée sur le marché.
